data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English 'Perca' meaning 'pier' or 'spear' and 'kin' meaning 'son of'. This name was commonly used in the Middle Ages. The name Perkin carries the meaning “Pier, Son of” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Perkin usually hope their child will grow to embody pier, son of and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Perkin' has a rich history in English literature and folklore. Notable figures with the name 'Perkin' include Perkin Warbeck, a pretender to the English throne in the late 15th century, and Perkin Elmer, a character in Henry Wadsworth Longfellow's epic poem "The Tales of a Wayside Inn." The name 'Perkin' also has connections to the Perkin Revolver, a handgun used extensively during the American Civil War.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Perkin' is rooted in Old English and has a connection to the themes of protection and strength. As a Christian name, it can be seen as a reminder of God's protective presence in our lives. The name also echoes the story of the spear-bearing Percinus, a Christian martyr in Ancient Rome whose name is derived from the same Old English roots. As such, 'Perkin' can be viewed as a name that carries both temporal and spiritual meaning, reminding us of God's strength and protection in the face of adversity.
